title: The explicit common interchange boundary in the product grid
statement: For finite A and two supplied diagrams, use F,G,H,BV,BW,E,K,R,P from [lem-pur-etale-graph-product-geometry]. The productLiftInterchange from F.functor followed by R(G.a) to R(H.a) J(E) R(R) is the inverse exchange for the Cartesian square B, with its two proper compositors. The productSquareInterchange from that word followed by J(G.e) R(G.p) to H.functor is the normalized exchange for the product square Q0, with open and proper compositors. productInterchange is their composite, from F.functor followed by G.functor to H.functor. All maps are these explicit isomorphisms, without any arbitrary choice of a map between the endpoints.

Elementary presentation move compared with upstream LowerShriekComposition.lean, rightDerivedLowerStarCompOpenImmersionLowerShriekIso and the eh factor in nonempty_iso_rightDerivedLowerShriek_comp. This is a new obligation, not a theorem claimed to be proved by that Lean existence declaration.

proof.text: Split the proper composite F.p G.a as BV R. Apply the inverse normalized exchange for B, and combine F.a BW=H.a. This defines productLiftInterchange. Apply the exchange for the product Q0, combine E K=H.e and P G.p=H.p, to define productSquareInterchange. Compose after the canonical associator to obtain productInterchange.
